layers.note: Lines streams, ponds and wet meadows.

moisture.note: Wet ground: stream banks, shores and swamps.

elevation_m.note: Sea level to about 1,000 m in western Washington; the upper limits are loose.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on flats and gentle slopes.

coldest_c.note: Very cold winters borne: coldest-month means from about −25 °C (gone by −35 °C), as across the boreal forest.

hard_freeze_c.note: Among the hardiest: lows to about −50 °C borne.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 11.5 to 27 °C; gone below 9 °C, where summers are too short, and above 30 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 1,100 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 700.

degree_days_5.note: A short growing season suffices: about 450 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 200.

moisture_index.note: It grows where the ground stays wet whatever the climate's moisture index, so only the driest climates (below about 0.1) rule it out; the site's own moisture places it.

summer_rain.note: No limit in its range: summer-dry coasts to continental summer rain.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands; not yet checked against the public-domain USDA references (Silvics of North America, the Fire Effects Information System, PLANTS). Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Red-osier dogwood grows across North America by streams and in wetlands (FEIS, the PLANTS Database). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
